title: Diameter of N-ary Tree
statement:
You are given a tree with `n` nodes numbered `0` to `n - 1`, where node `0` is the root. Each node may have any number of children. The tree is given as `n - 1` undirected edges.

The **diameter** of the tree is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes. The path does not have to pass through the root.

Print the diameter.

If you already know how to do this for a binary tree, think about what changes when a node has more than two children: you now need to keep track of the two tallest child branches, not just a left and a right one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
Each of the next `n - 1` lines contains two integers `u` and `v`, meaning there is an edge between nodes `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of edges on the longest path in the tree.
constraints: The number of nodes on any root-to-leaf path (rooted at node 0) is at most 5000, so recursive solutions fit in the call stack

examples.explanation: The path 4 - 2 - 1 - 3 - 5 uses 4 edges and does not touch the root 0. No longer path exists.
Node 0 is connected to every other node, so any path between two leaves goes leaf - 0 - leaf, which is 2 edges.
A single node has no edges, so the diameter is 0.

hints: Start with the binary-tree idea: the longest path whose highest node is v goes down through two different children of v, so its length is the sum of the two longest downward branches at v.
For every node compute the height of its tallest branch. For an N-ary node you only need the two largest child heights, so you do not need to sort the children.
Combine the two largest child heights at each node and take the maximum over all nodes. Because the edges are undirected, first figure out each node's parent by walking from node 0.
